transcript: Header: 2026-04-20 16:00 UTC | Duration: 42m | Recording: yes

Attendees: Samira Patel (Redwood AE), Ethan Ruiz (Redwood CSM), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE); Janelle Kim (Mariner Head of AI), Rajesh Menon (Mariner CTO), Lena Ortiz (Mariner DevOps), Tom Brady (Mariner PM)
Summary: Quarterly check-in to review usage, cost trends, recent reliability incidents, upcoming roadmap items, and next steps for potential dedicated capacity pilot.
Topics: usage & cost, reliability incidents (03/15 outage), VPC/private deployment questions, roadmap asks (pinning model versions, rollout policies), benchmark pilot

00:00 Samira: Hi everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate the time. Quick QBR agenda — usage and cost, reliability notes, roadmap items, then next steps. Janelle, do you want to kick off with how things are going on your side?

00:26 Janelle: Yeah thanks Samira. Overall things are good, we've increased traffic about 2.3x since January. Main thing — embeddings use spiked for semantic search; costs rose in March, we saw a 40% increase. A couple of times latency was higher than expected, users called it out.
00:52 Ethan: Got it. We pulled the per-route cost — I'll send that in the deck. Diego, do you want to walk through the reliability events?

01:07 Diego: Sure. We saw a shortfall on 2026-03-15 where two of the dedicated nodes in us-east experienced transient GPU OOMs after a big batch job. That triggered failover to hosted pool which kept requests alive but increased latency. Logs show KV cache pressure plus a large batched job. We recommended smaller batch caps and increasing KV cache reservation — Mariner implemented a temporary config change on 03/16.

01:42 Rajesh: Right. That incident was problematic because our internal healthchecks tripped and service wrote alerts. The fallback to hosted was fine for availability but we want consistent p95 latency. We're evaluating dedicated vs hosted with predictable throughput.

02:03 Diego: Totally reasonable. For predictable p95 we recommend Dedicated (reserved capacity) — you can pin model versions, have configured autoscaling policy, and avoid cross-tenant variability. We ran a quick sim last week and saw p95 drop from ~780ms to ~420ms under your workload shape when on a 4-GPU dedicated pool with optimized batching and prefix caching.
02:35 Lena: Quick Q — what's the effort to move to Private (VPC)? Our security team wants KMS integration and audit logs retained for 2 years, plus SAML SSO.

02:50 Samira: We have Private deployment options and enterprise package for that. KMS/HSM integrations are supported; audit logs and extended retention are an add-on. We'll share the security pack. For SAML we can do SP-initiated SSO and provisioning — Ethan will follow up for the admin contact.
03:12 Tom: On the roadmap side, we'd really like a canary rollout feature that can route a % of traffic to a new model and auto-roll back based on error/latency thresholds.

03:28 Diego: Good news — Redwood Console supports canary/A-B rollouts and automatic fallback policies. We'll demo it in the pilot. One note: define the metrics you care about (latency, error rate, quality) and we'll wire alerts.
03:45 Janelle: Also quality regression monitoring — last month we saw a drop in few templates after a model update, hard to debug. We want per-prompt evals tied to deployments.
04:01 Ethan: We can enable evaluation hooks and register a few golden prompts; the Console will show regressions post-deploy. We'll include that in the trial plan.
04:20 Rajesh: On costs — what levers should we try immediately? We're sensitive to both embedding and generation costs.

04:33 Diego: Quick wins: enable prefix/KV caching for routes that reuse context, reduce batch sizes on embeddings (or run them async with higher throughput), and try quantized model variants for lower-cost inference. Redwood Optimize can suggest model/quantization profiles by workload — we'll attach recommended settings.

05:02 Samira: We'll include a cost-by-workload spreadsheet showing tokens, embeddings calls, and per-route unit cost. Also a recommended Dedicated configuration with expected monthly commit and estimated savings vs hosted.
05:18 Lena: About the VPC - can we do VPC peering with our AWS account and also keep logs in our S3 bucket?

05:28 Diego: Yes — VPC peering supported, and audit logs can be exported to your S3 or Cloud Storage with lifecycle rules. For KMS you'll need to provide the key ARN and we'll integrate during onboarding.
05:47 Janelle: Timeline question — if we want dedicated pilot, how long to stand up?

05:55 Samira: For Dedicated pilot often 1-2 weeks once contract is signed; if you need Private (VPC/on-prem) it can be 3-6 weeks depending on networking and compliance gating. We'll scope the shortest path: start with Dedicated pilot in your account region, run benchmarks, then discuss Private if needed.
06:18 Rajesh: Are there SLA commitments for dedicated?
06:22 Ethan: Dedicated has SLA-backed uptime and latency targets; we'll include that language in the pack. For mission-critical we're happy to discuss higher SLAs as an add-on.
06:34 Tom: For the benchmark, can we test the three main routes — chat completion, few-shot summarization, and nightly embedding batch?
06:42 Diego: Absolutely. We'll configure the 3 routes, match your concurrency/sequence length distribution. We'll also capture KV cache hit/miss and per-token latencies.
06:54 Janelle: One last ops ask — more visibility on token-level cost per route in the Console, right now the breakdown is coarse.
07:03 Ethan: We're working on token-level cost breakdown per route in the next Console release; ETA Q2. I'll flag your use-case as priority — more granular attribution is in the roadmap.
07:18 Samira: Okay let's move to the Q&A — any other blockers?
07:25 Lena: We need a contact for SOC 2 audit material, and the timeline for getting copies of policies.
07:32 Ethan: I'll share the security pack and SOC 2 artifact access request; we can set up a short session with Security to go through specifics.
07:46 Rajesh: Cost sensitivity again — curious how much we save if we commit to a 6-month Dedicated reserve vs staying hosted. Rough ballpark?

07:58 Diego: For a 6-month commit for your observed monthly usage, we estimate ~28-35% reduction in per-token cost depending on model mix and enabling caching/quantization. Exact numbers in the spreadsheet.
08:15 Janelle: Perfect. Also can you confirm that we can pin model versions for the same endpoint? We rely on reproducibility for clinical notes generation.
08:25 Diego: Yes — you can pin model versions and the rollout policies can route traffic between versions while keeping the same endpoint URL. We'll show it in demo.

08:38 Samira: Quick recap and next steps: Samira sends slide deck + cost spreadsheet; Diego runs dedicated benchmark and shares logs; Ethan shares security pack and kicks off SSO/KMS onboarding; Mariner to share VPC diagram and admin contacts. Any additions?
08:58 Tom: Nothing else from product side. We're good to proceed with the pilot proposal.
09:05 Janelle: One small note — can we get an export of last 6 months of usage per-route as csv?
09:12 Ethan: Yes I'll export and share by EOD tomorrow.
09:20 Samira: Great. We'll follow up with a proposed SOW for the pilot and scheduling for the benchmark. Thanks everyone — we'll send notes and items after the call.
09:30 Meeting end: 16:42 UTC
Notes: occasional transcription artifacts noted (product names like 'KV cache' sometimes transcribed as 'K V cash'), we kept the raw speaker labels as recorded.
